findings.title: Organization disabled prevents login cache invalidation when updating or removing an organization-linked IDP
findings.body: `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` (and `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` on remove) uses `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to decide whether the IDP qualifies for login. In `update()`, `original` (`idpById`) is obtained via `getById(...)`, which wraps the model with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. That wrapper overrides `isEnabled()` to return `false` whenever the linked organization is currently disabled. Meanwhile, the JPA `getForLogin` query populates the login cache based on the database column `enabled = true` without checking whether the organization is enabled. Consequently, if an organization is temporarily disabled while an IDP linked to it is in the login cache, any update to that IDP (such as disabling it, setting `hideOnLogin = true`, setting `BROKER_PUBLIC = false`, or unlinking it from the organization) or removing it sees `getLoginPredicate().test(original) == false` and skips invalidating the login cache. If the organization is later re-enabled, `getForLogin` will continue serving stale cached results containing the disabled, hidden, or unlinked IDP.

findings.title: Test cleanup registers literal "alias" instead of the created IDP's alias
findings.body: In `testCacheIDPForLogin` (lines 381 and 425), cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` using the literal string `"alias"` instead of the actual alias of the created identity provider (`"idp-alias-" + i` and `"idp-alias-20"`). As a result, the 20+ identity providers created during this test are never removed after the test finishes and will leak into subsequent tests in the suite.
